variants.title: Harmonics of a square wave on a CRO
variants.sample: Square wave, 1 kHz, ±2 V (generic function generator)
variants.unknown: the relative amplitudes of the harmonics
variants.note: Only odd harmonics, with amplitudes 4A/(nπ): they fall as 1/n.

source.title: Fourier series of standard waveforms (Arfken and Weber, Mathematical Methods for Physicists); generic bench signal, 1 kHz

variants.title: Harmonics of a triangular wave on a CRO
variants.sample: Triangular wave, 1 kHz, ±2 V (generic function generator)
variants.unknown: the relative amplitudes of the harmonics
variants.note: Only odd harmonics, with amplitudes 8A/(n²π²): they fall as 1/n², so the wave is nearly a sine.

source.title: Fourier series of standard waveforms (Arfken and Weber, Mathematical Methods for Physicists); generic bench signal, 1 kHz

variants.title: Harmonics of a clipped sine wave on a CRO
variants.sample: Sine wave of ±2 V clipped flat at ±1 V, 1 kHz (generic bench signal)
variants.unknown: the relative amplitudes of the harmonics
variants.note: Clipping a sine at half its height adds odd harmonics: the third is about 23 % of the fundamental.

source.title: Fourier series of standard waveforms (Arfken and Weber, Mathematical Methods for Physicists); generic bench signal, 1 kHz
